Updated}} }} {{Quote|So, basically, what the magistrate is saying is that we're looking for a needle in a literal ''planet'' full of haystacks''.|Mace Windu, to Aayla Secura|}} '''Mina-Rau''', or '''Xuretria''', was an [[Agriworld|agricultural]] [[planet]] located in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]' [[D'Astan sector]]. It was home to an expansive farming industry with councils and settlements dotted among it. During the [[Republic Era|days]] of the [[Galactic Republic]], the world was victim to [[Raids on Mina-Rau|raids]] from the [[Quillian bandits]], which were driven off by [[Jedi Master]] [[Fondar Etzis]]. However, the [[assassin]] [[Corlis Rath]] [[Death|murdered]] with a [[Emubara|poison]] Etzis to draw out Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn]]. Jinn went to Mina-Rau with fellow [[Jedi]] [[Mace Windu]] and [[Aayla Secura]], finding evidence that Etzis was poisoned. However, Rath was able to single out Jinn for a [[Duel on Mina-Rau|duel]], ending with the assassin [[poison]]ing the Jedi. Windu and Secura took Jinn offworld in a critical condition to cure him. By the [[Imperial Era|time]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Mina-Rau's harvests relied a lot on undocumented workers, the Empire being known to let this slide. A group of [[Technician|mechanics]] who had fled [[Ferrix occupation|Imperial occupation]] resided in [[Council 207]], befriending others in the local community like [[Kellen]]. However, the Empire conducted an [[Imperial Supply Census]] in [[4 BBY]], arresting any undocumented that ran away as they went council by council. The mechanics kept track of the situation via Kellen and stayed cautious, but one of them, [[Bix Caleen]], caught the [[eye]] of Imperial [[Lieutenant]] [[Krole]]. When the Imperial auditing was set on their council, the mechanics made preparations to head to [[Eight Hundred Block]] on a fake work order provided by Kellen. However, Imperial forces moved into the area before they could leave. While the mechanic [[Brasso]] was arrested by Imperial troops, Caleen had another visit from Krole, who assaulted her. Caleen ended up killing Krole, and the mechanic and [[Axis network|rebel spy]] [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]] arrived to Mina-Rau in a [[Theft of the TIE Avenger prototype|stolen]] [[TIE Avenger prototype]] and [[Skirmish on Mina-Rau|attacked]] the Imperials holding Brasso. Caleen and the mechanic [[Wilmon Paak]] escaped with Andor, but Brasso was killed. ==Description== {{Quote|This is an ''agrarian'' world. One replete with all forms of insect and plant life.|Aayla Secura, to Mace Windu|}} [[File:Mina-Rau-SWmap.png|thumb|left|300px|Mina-Rau was situated along the Celanon Spur.]] Mina-Rau,{{Databank|mina-rau|Mina-Rau}} also known as Xuretria,[[Jedi Knights 9|''Jedi Knights'' 9]] was a terrestrial [[planet]] located in the [[Mina-Rau system]] within the [[New Territories]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. Situated in the [[D'Astan sector]] at the coordinates O-6 on the [[Standard Galactic Grid]], the world lay along the [[Celanon Spur]] [[hyperspace route]] between the [[Celanon system|Celanon]] and [[Ord Cestus system]]s.{{StarWarsGalaxyMap}} Appearing sandy-[[color]]ed from above,[[Jedi Knights 7|''Jedi Knights'' 7]] Mina-Rau had a Type I Atmosphere breathable to [[human]]s and other [[species]]. The planet's surface consisted of large fields, hills, grasslands, and lakes. Many different forms of [[plant]]s and [[insect]]s were present on the world, as well as the gentle and dependable [[Mina-Rau bier beast]]s.{{Databank|mina-rau-bier-beast|Mina-Rau bier beast}} ==History== ===Reign of the Republic=== ====Rath's bait==== {{Quote|My understanding is that Master Etzis' assignment to Mina-Rau was a ''recent'' one…''"
"''Yes. He was ''instrumental'' in dealing with a group of ''bandits'' who had been stealing our crop yield.|Aayla Secura and Magistrate Khediva, on Fondar Etzis' importance to Mina-Rau|}} [[File:CombinesAtWork-JediKnights6.png|thumb|right|300px|Mina-Rau was active as an agriworld during the Republic's reign, where combine machines would aid harvesting.]] [[Farmer]]s worked on Mina-Rau by the [[Republic Era|time]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]. As an [[agriworld]], the planet produced harvests of [[grain]] with the help of [[Combine (Mina-Rau)|combine machines]]. Between [[40 BBY]] and [[34 BBY]],The events of [[Jedi Knights 6|''Jedi Knights'' 6]] take place between [[40 BBY]] and [[34 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:JediKnightsDate|here]]. the planet was governed at least in part by [[Magistrate]] [[Khediva]], but the world saw [[Raids on Mina-Rau|incursions]] from the [[Quillian bandits]], who used [[speeder]]s and stole from the planet's harvest. In response, the people of Mina-Rau were provided protection by [[Jedi Master]] [[Fondar Etzis]], who was greatly effective in fighting off the bandits and quickly became a beloved part of their community. However, Etzis was targeted by the [[assassin]] [[Corlis Rath]], who sought to draw out another Jedi Master named [[Qui-Gon Jinn]]. Rath was on a personal crusade to [[Death|kill]] Jinn over a grudge that had began when the two were [[Youngling|young]][[Jedi Knights 10|''Jedi Knights'' 10]] and had attacked the [[Jedi]] on the planet [[Vekura]].[[Jedi Knights 1|''Jedi Knights'' 1]] The assassin thus [[poison]]ed Etzis with the [[emubara]] toxin. Despite the mysterious circumstances around Etzis' death, Khediva was certain the bandits were not responsible due to his successes against them and, instead, believed the Jedi Master had simply died of old age. In response to his death, an honor guard of Jedi—consisting of Jinn, Jedi Master [[Mace Windu]], and [[Jedi Knight]] [[Aayla Secura]]—travelled to Mina-Rau in a [[T-6 shuttle]] to recover Etzis' remains and deliver them to the planet''[[The Living Force]]'' [[Coruscant]], the home of the [[Jedi Order]]'s primary [[Imperial Palace|Temple]], for cremation. Khediva led the group into a [[Unidentified location (Mina-Rau)|urban area]] in the midst of a harvest, which the magistrate briefly spoke about with Secura. Khediva brought the Jedi to Etzis's body, discussing the possible causes of the late Jedi Master's death. When the Jedi trio inspected the body, Jinn sensed darkness around his remains, concluding that Etzis must have been murdered. Jinn's associates did not sense anything, but Jinn himself took a [[blood]]-sample from the body to further pursue his prediction. The three went to Etzis's [[Fondar Etzis's starship|starship]], finding no disturbance. Jinn, though, examined the blood sample on a terminal and found traces of the toxin Rath used. The group agreed that it could not have been the bandits that had done it. Later, as the Jedi drew more conclusions from the ship's logs, Khediva found it hard to believe who on Mina-Rau would want to kill Etzis. ====Rath's wrath==== {{Quote|You killed Master Etzis, didn't you? You ''poisoned'' him. To draw me out. To bring me ''here''. Why? So you can ''kill'' me?|Qui-Gon Jinn fights Carlis Rath|}} [[File:Jinnlightsaberswing-JediKnights6.png|thumb|left|350px|Corlis Rath attacked Qui-Gon Jinn in Mina-Rau's fields.]] The Jedi made their way into the fields, where Secura theorized an element natural to Mina-Rau—something the indigenous population was immune to but could be fatal to an offworlder—had been responsible for Etzis's death. However, Rath, armed with emubara-coated, energy-edged [[Sword|blades]],{{StoryCite|story=The Moon of Death|book=Free Comic Book Day 2025: Star Wars 1|bformatted=Free Comic Book Day 2025: ''Star Wars'' 1}} stalked the group at that moment, Jinn sensing his presence. Despite Jinn's warning, Windu and Secura, who again did not sense anything, were shot with [[tranquilizer dart]]s. Rath then attacked Jinn, the pair fighting in Mina-Rau's fields. When a combine approached them, they leapt onto the massive vehicle and continued to fight on it. As they fought, Jinn deduced Rath's plan to draw him out, questioning why the assassin was trying to kill him. When the Jedi successfully disarmed the Rath, the latter finally mentioned [[Sinsara]], the planet where Rath's grudge on Jinn originated. This shocked Jinn, so much that the assassin could stab him with the emubara-laced blades and flee. Bleeding out, Jinn fell unconscious. After regaining their own consciousness, Windu and Secura found their fallen comrade, finding that he had been poisoned. As the pair considered options, the unconscious Jinn muttered Sinsara. The Jedi Master was thus taken back to the group's [[shuttle]] and stabilised with [[dothrasim]]. Secura determined what Sinsara was, and thus she and Windu took the shuttle there, where they eventually acquired the antidote to save Jinn. Jinn eventually woke up more healed on Coruscant, reflecting on the details of his last conscious moments, on Mina-Rau. The Jedi Master thus, journeyed to Sinsara himself to [[Duel on Sinsara|finally end]] his struggle with Rath. ===Reign of the Empire=== ====Uneasy industry==== {{Quote|We've been counting visas. It's a tough spot for everyone. The Councils need help or there's no harvest. The help is undocumented.|Krole, on Mina-Rau's workforce|}} In [[19 BBY]], the Republic [[Proclamation of the New Order|transitioned]] into the [[Galactic Empire]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' During the Empire's [[Imperial Era|reign]], farmers worked on the planet to produce grain for the [[Politics|government]]. The entire planet, by that time, had been terraformed to grow that specific type of grain for the Empire, which made use of the food on Coruscant, which had become the capital of the Empire and prospered greatly from the extracted labor and resources of outlying planets.''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' People who worked on Mina-Rau were required by law to have either shares or visas. Despite this, the Councils hired undocumented immigrants as well to ensure harvests were possible. The Empire, while aware that many residents lacked visas or shares, was also known to overlook such violations to maintain agricultural output. The planet was subjected to the [[Imperial Supply Census]], where the Empire inspected grain exports and the visas of those residing on the planet, one taking place around [[14 BBY]].{{Andor|Sagrona Teema}} establishes that the [[Galactic Empire]] conducted an [[Imperial Supply Census]] ten [[Standard year|years]] before the events of the episode, which {{SW|url=news/andor-season-2-costume-design|text=The Costumes of ''Andor'' Season 2}} dates to [[4 BBY]]. This census must have therefore taken place around [[14 BBY]]. Imperial [[Lieutenant]] [[Krole]] visited the world at some point and visited the [[city]] of [[Rau]]. [[File:KellenUpdate-Andor202.png|thumb|right|300px|Kellen befriended the undocumented mechanics.]] Sometime after the [[Ferrix occupation|Imperial occupation]] of their [[homeworld]], [[Ferrix]], in [[5 BBY]],{{AndorDate|1}} the humans [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]], [[Bix Caleen]], [[Wilmon Paak]], and [[Brasso]], and their [[droid]] [[B2EMO]], relocated to Mina-Rau, finding work as [[Technician|mechanics]] and hiding among the Mina-Rau farming community. Keeping their past undercover,{{InsiderCite|233|Andor Season 2 Companion|''Andor'' Season 2 Companion}} they lived in a [[mobil-haus]] in [[Council 207]] and were friends with the store owner [[Kellen]]. Andor at the least secretly worked for a [[Axis network|rebel network]] operated by the [[spy]] [[Luthen Rael]]. Over time, Caleen had reoccurring nightmares of an [[Gorst|Imperial interrogator]] who [[torture]]d her on Ferrix.{{Andor|Nobody's Listening!}} While Brasso began a relationship with the documented worker [[Talia (Mina-Rau)|Talia]], Paak also got close to Kellen's daughter, [[Beela]]. This was much to the disapproval of Beela's [[Parent|mother]], [[Aneth]], as Paak was undocumented. ====Imperial audit==== {{Dialogue|Bix Caleen|What are they doing?|Brasso|An Imperial Supply Census. It's an audit. A spot check. They wanna know what they've got, where it's coming from.|Wilon Paak|What about who's doing it?|Brasso|He's ''[Kellen]'' asking. I guess right now, they're focused on Council Five Hundred. That's what we saw out there today.|Bix Caleen|If they're checking visas, we have a problem.|attr=Bix Caleen, Brasso, and Wilmon Paak discuss the Empire's presence on Mina-Rau|src=}} [[File:ImpsArrive-Andor201.png|thumb|left|300px|Imperial forces arrive at Mina-Rau.]] In [[4 BBY]], an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] arrived above Mina-Rau and another Imperial Supply Census began on the planet, leading to a comms blackout to ensure the audit could be conducted properly. Imperial presence arrived as Beela carried [[water]] to Caleen and Paak, who were repairing a sprinkler. Kellen and Brasso observed auditing take place at [[Council Five Hundred]], the latter heading back to the mobil-haus to discuss the situation with the other mechanics and Talia. Paak attempted to contact Andor, to no avail. As the audit went on and the Imperials caught an individual trying to flee from Five Hundred, [[Kellen's friend]] there updated him on the Empire's progress there and the store owner went to update the mechanics when his stock delivery arrived at the general store. As the group discussed if the Empire would bother to arrest undocumented workers like them, Kellen warned against trying to run. Imperial troops soon arrived at the general store for a visit, interrupting a private conversation between Paak and Beela in the fields. While [[soldier]]s looked around the general store, Lieutenant Krole went to the silos and greeted Caleen while she worked. Trying to make conversation with the nervous mechanic, the [[Imperial officer]] spoke about the Rau, inviting her to join him there. Caleen pretended to have a [[Marriage|husband]], leading Krole to ask questions about the alleged individual until Brasso arrived. The lieutenant questioned where they were based, leaving afterwards. As the inspections elsewhere continued, Kellen learned from a soldier that they would be moving on soon. The store owner discussed this with the mechanics that night, warning them that most the arrests were people trying to run. Kellen advised his friends to wait and see and be prepared. Imperials did an sweep of [[Council Six Hundred]], finding a group hiding. Hearing that his area would be next on the audit, Kellen forged a work order for [[Eight Hundred Block]] and went to Brasso, updating him on the situation. Kellen advised his friend that he and the other mechanics should leave that night and circle round when the inspection moved on. The store owner further stressed to Brasso to make sure Luthen Rael, whom neither of them knew the name of, knew what was happening on Mina-Rau. Meanwhile, Andor, who had been [[Yavin 4 turf war|held up]] elsewhere, learned about the communications blackout at Mina-Rau and began making his way there in a [[Theft of the TIE Avenger prototype|stolen]] [[TIE Avenger prototype]]. ====The escape==== {{Quote|Hey, did you see that ship go by?''"
"''I keep hoping it's gonna be Cassian.''"
"''I don't think we should wait till sundown. They're sweeping the far fields. And they'll be coming back. We could get pinned down here. We gotta move.|Brasso and Bix Caleen|}} [[File:ImpsArrive-Andor203.png|thumb|right|300px|Krole's forces arrive at the general store.]] The three mechanics got to packing their items in preparation to move to Eight Hundred at sundown. Brasso went to say goodbye to B2EMO at the communal eating area, wishing to leave him with Talia for the time being, when a [[TIE/rp Reaper attack lander]] flew over them on a sweep of the fields. Brasso returned to Caleen suggesting that they may have to move sooner. Paak had gone to say goodbye to Beela, so Brasso went to find him. While Paak was speaking with Beela, Krole and his troops arrived at the general store again. Ordering Aneth to feed his soldiers, Krole promised to be back in an hour and left [[Sergeant]] [[Stang (individual)|Stang]] in charge. The lieutenant went in [[Unit One (Galactic Empire)|one]] of their [[transport]]s, driven by [[Corporal]] [[Pyke (individual)|Pyke]], towards the mechanics' mobil-haus to see Caleen again. While Paak ran back towards the mobil-haus, Brasso took a speeder towards the general store and began sneaking around to find Paak, only to be arrested by two [[stormtrooper]]s. Brasso was taken back to the general store before Stang, pretending to be mad at Kellen in order to keep his friend's cover. Meanwhile, Krole arrived to greet Caleen, looking around the mobil-haus. Revealing that he knew she was illegal, he attempted to use this as leverage and tried to rape her. Resisting, Caleen scuffled with Krole until she gave him two blows with a tool. At the transport, Pyke heard Krole's subsequent screams and contacted Stang's [[Unit Two (Galactic Empire)|transport]] for help before approaching the mobil-haus with a [[blaster pistol]] drawn. After a fatally injured Krole stumbled out and died, Pyke tried to confront Caleen. Paak fired at the corporal, who was ultimately shot dead by Caleen. [[File:That-must-have-Stang-Andor203.png|thumb|left|300px|Cassian Andor engages the Empire's forces on Mina-Rau.]] Andor arrived at Mina-Rau and began descending towards the area where his friends were. Having received Pyke's call, Stang put together a unit to go to the corporal's aid. However, Andor swooped down in his TIE Avenger and [[Skirmish on Mina-Rau|destroyed]] the transport. As Brasso tried to get away on his speeder under fire from the remaining Imperial troops, Andor proceeded to eliminate those soldiers. It was too late, though, as Brasso was fatally shot, Andor finding him dead when he landed the fighter. Having seen the TIE Avenger's actions from afar, Caleen and Paak made their way to it and reunited with Andor. The three then fled Mina-Rau in the fighter. ====Caleen's sunrise==== {{Quote|G-g-go again. Once m-m-more and I win.|B2EMO plays with ARG19 on Mina-Rau|}} [[File:Bix-Child-JedhaKyberErso.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Bix Caleen walks through Mina-Rau's fields with her newborn child.]] Andor continued work under Rael afterwards with Caleen and Paak. By [[3 BBY]], Andor and Caleen were in a romantic relationship{{Andor|Ever Been to Ghorman?}} and in [[2 BBY]]{{AndorDate|209}} the former considered leaving the [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|rising rebellion]] against the Empire with Caleen. However, Caleen left first in order to force Andor to stay with the rebellion,{{Andor|Welcome to the Rebellion}} which was in the process of formalising at the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]. Caleen would go on to return to Mina-Rau{{Andor|Jedha, Kyber, Erso}} by [[1 BBY]]{{AndorDate|212}} and began raising her and Andor's [[Bix Caleen's child|newborn child]]. On one day that year, Caleen walked her child out into the fields as Talia and other workers cleared away at the communal dining area and B2EMO played with his droid friend [[ARG19]].{{Databank|arg19|ARG19}} ==Inhabitants== {{Quote|But, masters, please remember, Mina-Rau is a farming world, inhabited by simple farming folk. If there is one among our number capable of ''murder'', I strain to imagine who it could be.|Khediva|}} [[File:MinaRauDining-Andor203.png|thumb|left|300px|Workers dine on Mina-Rau.]] Mina-Rau was populated by many humans and at least [[Unidentified species (Mina-Rau)|one]] other species. Many workers hired by the Councils there did not have shares or visas, but were needed nonetheless to make sure the harvests could be carried out. Khediva described the population as simple farming folk, some of which, as Krole learned, went their whole lives without visiting the city of Rau. ==Locations== {{Quote|Have you been to the Rau? Some of these farmers live their whole lives and never go. It's not much of a city, but you'd think over time, they'd get curious.|Krole, to Bix Caleen|}} [[File:MinaRauLandscape-Andor201.png|thumb|right|300px|Mina-Rau had many settlements on hills.]] Mina-Rau's settlements were divided into councils and blocks, some being built on hills that rose above the grain fields. These included Council 207, [[Council Three Hundred]], [[Council 436]], Council Five Hundred, Council Six Hundred, and Eight Hundred Block. The city of Rau and a settlement where Etzis's body was briefly kept were also located on the world. Krole noted after having dinner in the Rau that the city had changed since he visited a few years before. Other notable locations included the general store ran by Kellen and his family, as well as the mobil-haus where the undocumented mechanics resided for some time. ==Behind the scenes== ===Media debuts=== {{Quote|For Mina-Rau, all we had was a couple sketches of Luke Hull's wonderful wheat sketches. I hadn't seen Mina-Rau yet. I didn't know what the hell it was. But I'm gonna say this until someone adds it to the Wikipedia page, Tony Gilroy named Mina-Rau after my daughter, Mina. He made a ''Star Wars''-loving little girl immensely happy.|Tom Bissell, on Mina-Rau|{{WebCite|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/andor/andor-season-2-finale-postmortem-with-writer-tom-bissell|text=''Andor'' Season 2 Finale Postmortem with Writer Tom Bissell|work=[[Wikipedia:Paste (magazine)|Paste Magazine]]|date=2025-05-14|archivedate=20250517151322}}}} [[File:MobilHausExterior-BtS.png|thumb|right|300px|Exterior filming of the mobil-haus on Mina-Rau]] Mina-Rau first appeared in "[[One Year Later]]," "[[Sagrona Teema]]," and "[[Harvest]]," the first three-episode arc of the [[Andor Season 2|second season]] of [[Tony Gilroy]]'s live-action [[Disney+]] series ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'', which aired on [[April 22]], [[2025]]. The world was first visually revealed prior to the release of the episodes in a sizzle reel for the series exclusively shown at [[Wikipedia:D23 (Disney)|D23 Expo]] on [[August 12]], [[2024]].{{SW|url=news/d23-brasil-andor-season-2-premiere-date-announce|text=D23 Brasil 2024: ''Andor'' Premiere Date Revealed and Other ''Star Wars'' News}} Its name was then first mentioned in a production brief linked to the show and was released by [[The Walt Disney Company|Walt Disney Studios]] via [[Wikipedia:Getty Images|Getty Images]] on [[April 10]], 2025.{{Getty|url=thewaltdisneystudios/allaccess/#!asset/9rcqp87xgvc64ts3kgchk48|text=ANDOR S2 Production Brief FINAL 2 4-10-25|author=[[The Walt Disney Company|The Walt Disney Studios]]|date=2025-04-10}} Mina-Rau was a setting in the [[Jedi Knights 6|sixth]] and [[Jedi Knights 7|seventh]] issues of [[Marc Guggenheim]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knights]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]], both penciled by [[Madibek Musabekov]] and published by [[Marvel Comics]] on [[August 13]]{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/122257/star_wars_jedi_knights_2025_6|text=Star Wars: Jedi Knights (2025) #6}} and [[September 10]] of 2025 respectively.{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/122258/star_wars_jedi_knights_2025_7|text=Star Wars: Jedi Knights (2025) #7}} In the [[Jedi Knights 9|ninth issue]], released on [[November 19]] of that year,{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/122260/star_wars_jedi_knights_2025_9|text=Star Wars: Jedi Knights (2025) #9}} the planet was referred to entirely as Xuretria. This article assumes that this is just an alternate name. ===Utopian visions=== {{Quote|I wanted to get some sunshine in the show and some bright sunlight. Where does all the food come from for Coruscant? They've been cast out of a community that they really care about, and they found a new place to be, and it's sunny and it's wonderful, and it's going to be taken away from them.|Tony Gilroy, on the conception of Mina-Rau|}} [[File:GeneralStore-Declassified.png|thumb|left|300px|Concept art of the Mina-Rau General Store]] Mina-Rau was conceived to be the new home for the characters that had left Ferrix, and indeed it mirrored the other planet in its tightly knit community built upon a local economy that was driven by hard labor. Gilroy, who wrote the three episode arc, intended to bring some "bright sunlight" to the series by conveying Mina-Rau as a peaceful and friendly place that he would like to live in, but also where Bix Caleen could still be suffering. He wanted its community to be successful as to follow along with the show's themes of community, as well as the destruction of community. For the latter part, Gilroy wanted the characters' new life on Mina-Rau to be taken away again, including the death of Brasso, to drive their motivations forward.{{SW|url=news/andor-season-2-interview-tony-gilroy|text=Making a Revolutionary: Inside ''Andor'' Season 2 with Tony Gilroy}} Concept art for Mina-Rau was conceived by at least the artists [[Alex Dudar]] and [[Chester Carr]],{{SW|url=news/andor-concept-to-screen|text=Taking ''Andor'' from Concept to Screen}} with executive producer [[Luke Hull]] also contributing some sketches. For the planet's return in "[[Jedha, Kyber, Erso]]," the final episode of the series released on [[May 13]] of 2025, episode writer [[Tom Bissell]] had only Hull's wheat sketches to work around as the setting for revisiting Bix Caleen and B2EMO. According to Bissell, Gilroy named the planet after the writer's own daughter, Mina. ''Andor''{{'s}} costume designer [[Michael Wilkinson]] designed the clothing of Mina-Rau with a distinct colour palette, textures and silhouettes. He assigned the theme of workwear to Mina-Rau, his textile team developing the clothing with [[Wikipedia:Japan|Japanese]] [[Wikipedia:Sashiko|sashiko]] stitching and handblocked patterns. To add to the theme, the clothing was heavily worn by the textile team, and featured with lots of repairs.{{Instagram|username=michaelwilkinson|url=p/DLz_8awRQ_-|name=[[Michael Wilkinson]]|date=2025-07-07|archiveurl=https://archive.is/8lVHO}} ===Production set-backs=== {{Quote|Somehow we found a farmer and convinced them to grow that instead of wheat that year across their field. Rich Hill, location manager, found a very good field, actually, not too far from the studios. It gave us great…horizon lines because obviously it had to look vast. We had to extend all this in post as well.|Luke Hull, on the set of Mina-Rau|}} [[File:MinaRauLunch-BtS.png|thumb|right|300px|A roughly 200 acre field's worth of ancient rye was grown for the set of Mina-Rau.]] For the set of Mina-Rau, production intended to grow its own field of a single crop to use for filming. Location manager [[Rich Hill]], found a roughly 200 acre field{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-creator-season-2-episodes-1236190457|text='Andor' Creator Tony Gilroy Talks the Challenges of Following Up Season One's Rapturous Acclaim|author=Brian Davids|date=2025-04-15|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|The Hollywood Reporter]]|archivedate=20250723042708}} near the village of [[Wikipedia:Watlington, Oxfordshire|Watlington]], [[Wikipedia:Oxfordshire|Oxfordshire]], not far from the studios, which had great horizon lines to make the planet's fields look vaster. Hull chose the crop grown to be an ancient [[Wikipedia:Rye|rye]] that could be grown in [[Wikipedia:England|England]] and convinced the farmer in charge to grow that across the field for the year instead of [[Wikipedia:Wheat|wheat]]. The mobil-haus was built as a full interior and exterior set, having to be disassembled and reassembled in [[Pinewood Studios]] due to torrential rain.{{SW|url=news/andor-trivia-guide-week-1|text=Secrets from the Set of ''Andor'' Season 2: Week 1 Trivia}} Before the main unit shoot could take place for Mina-Rau upon the blossoming of the rye, the [[Wikipedia:2023 SAG-AFTRA strike|SAG-AFTRA strikes]] began in summer [[2023]]. The rye field was left to continue growing, but the set was gradually relocated to Pinewood Studios, including led to a second relocation of the mobil-haus set to Pinewood Studios. When the time came, the rye was harvested and preserved in sheets of [[Wikipedia:Polystyrene|polystyrene]] at within a soundstage at the studios. The outdoor sets were then reconstructed on Pinewood's 007 stage in early 2024, and the Mina-Rau scenes, as well as the season's filming as a whole, were completed in that same portion of the year. In post-production, [[Industrial Light & Magic]] had their scanline VFX team working on Mina-Rau.{{ILM|url=andor-star-wars-ilm-tj-falls-mohen-leo-interview|text="Like Eating an Elephant One Bite at a Time": TJ Falls and Mohen Leo on the Visual Effects of 'Andor' Season 2}} During this phase, the fields were made to look more expansive. [[File:Brasso-Speeder-ILM.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The setup for the filming of Brasso's speeder on Mina-Rau]] The Imperial ''Gozanti''-class cruiser appearing above Mina-Rau in "One Year Later" was adapted from the model used in "[[Chapter 11: The Heiress]],"{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 11: The Heiress}} the third episode in the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|second season]] of the live-action Disney+ show ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' which aired on [[December 11]], [[2020]].{{InsiderCite|202|Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season Two Companion|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two Companion}} The Mina-Rau bier beasts were based on unused designs from [[Andor Season 1|''Andor'' Season 1]], originally intended for cattle on the planet{{Databank|aldhani|Aldhani}} [[Aldhani]]. These creatures were brought to life by two puppeteers operating a pair of legs each, adding a tangible realism to the scenes.
